title: Update-proof event ticketing for WordPress agencies
subtitle: Scratch-mode deep run. Scouted 7 niches from 23 HN seeds and marketplace reviews of 31 Shopify apps and 18 WordPress plugins, then mined 842 records on WordPress event ticketing.

verdict.summary: The pain is real and well documented: on WordPress.org, small organizers and their agencies say events plugin updates break ticket sales, paid support goes silent and renewals jump 50%. But the obvious fix, a hosted checkout that looks native on WordPress, already exists (Ticket Spot, with only 40+ installs; Ticket Tailor's embed). Nonprofits get ticketing free from Zeffy, and the WordPress.org forums forbid promotion, so organizer-direct scores 55. Pivot to WordPress agencies managing many small-org sites (57 on paper, untested) and run the 7-day agency test before building anything.

opportunities.name: Update-proof ticketing for WordPress agencies (pivot A′)
opportunities.one_liner: Hosted ticket checkout that looks native on clients' WordPress sites, sold to agencies at one flat price.
opportunities.why: The agency buyer has evidence behind it: agencies report updates crashing client sites (a1, a2), are pulling plugins from the sites they built (a3), and hold multiple licences (a4). Ticket Spot already sells the organizer-facing version (k1), so the gap is narrow (4). Reach is unproven: WordPress.org forums forbid promotion (k8). A hypothesis to test, not a proven gap.

opportunities.name: Shopify packing-slip and invoice printing
opportunities.one_liner: Reliable bulk order printing for Order Printer refugees.
opportunities.why: 172 of 380 Order Printer reviews are 1-star (s4, s5), but Order Printer Pro is rated 4.9 across 2,989 reviews. Scored at scout depth. Pain is capped at 6 because the evidence is a single review page, short of the rubric's 2+ sources for 7+. Reach is held at 6 because free places to pitch weren't checked at scout depth.

opportunities.one_liner: Simple digital delivery after SendOwl's price change.
opportunities.why: SendOwl's price complaints (s10, s11) and regressions in Shopify's own app (s12), but Filemonk and Sky Pilot are rated 4.8 to 4.9. Scored at scout depth. Pain is capped at 6 because the evidence is a single review page, short of the rubric's 2+ sources for 7+. Reach is held at 6 because free places to pitch weren't checked at scout depth.

opportunities.name: Update-proof ticket checkout for small WordPress organizers (A)
opportunities.one_liner: Hosted checkout and monitored ticket delivery, embedded natively in the organizer's own WordPress site.
opportunities.why: Pain is strong and repeated by many authors across 8 plugins: updates break sales (r1, r2), support goes silent (r6, r8), renewal prices jump (r9, r10). Buyers already pay $99 to $399/yr (c2, c4). But the critic found Ticket Spot already selling this exact pitch with 40+ installs (k1, k2), Ticket Tailor claims an embedded WordPress checkout (k5), and Zeffy is free for nonprofits (k7). Gap 3, reach 5.

opportunities.name: Shopify search after Search & Discovery regressions
opportunities.one_liner: Exact-match/SKU search for small Shopify catalogs.
opportunities.why: Fresh 2026 complaints (s1, s2, s3) from one review page only. Loved paid apps rated 4.7 to 4.9 already exist (scout table). Scored at scout depth. Pain is capped at 6 because the evidence is a single review page, short of the rubric's 2+ sources for 7+. Reach is held at 6 because free places to pitch weren't checked at scout depth.

opportunities.name: Shopify bundles with variants
opportunities.one_liner: Bundles that handle variants without a stack of paid apps.
opportunities.why: Shopify Bundles is rated 2.8 (s6, s7), but Simple Bundles and Bundler are both rated 4.9. Scored at scout depth. Pain is capped at 6 because the evidence is a single review page, short of the rubric's 2+ sources for 7+. Reach is held at 6 because free places to pitch weren't checked at scout depth.

opportunities.name: Cookie consent after free tiers went paid
opportunities.one_liner: A free-feeling cookie banner for WordPress.
opportunities.why: The complaint is that it should be free (s16, s17), so willingness to pay is low, and compliance liability comes with it.

gap.statement: Small organizers who sell tickets from their own WordPress site can't get a checkout that keeps working through updates and reliably delivers tickets at a small, predictable price, because every plugin runs checkout inside their WordPress (where updates break it) and every hosted option charges per ticket or drops an off-brand embed on their page. Critic note: Ticket Spot already targets this exact gap (k1), so the remaining opening is the agency buyer.

critic.risk: The exact product already exists: Ticket Spot sells a hosted, update-proof WordPress checkout to churches and theatres (k1, k4), and Ticket Tailor claims an embedded WordPress checkout (k5).
A free incumbent covers big segments: Zeffy is free for nonprofits (k7), and Ticket Tailor lets organizers pass fees to buyers (k6).
The pain may not convert to payment: the exact fix has only 40+ WordPress.org installs (k2), and ticket-delivery failures are rare in the corpus.
The channel is closed: WordPress.org forums, where buyers complain, forbid promotion (k8).
Ticketing platforms that held funds failed and left organizers unpaid (k9, k10, k12), so buyers distrust new vendors.
critic.rebuttal: Direct charges into each client's own Stripe account mean no ticket money ever sits with us (k4 shows the model), and all data is exportable.

critic.risk: Chargeback and refund liability, plus event-night on-call for a 10-hour-a-week founder.
critic.rebuttal: Avoid destination charges, where the platform is liable (k11). Use direct charges on clients' own Standard accounts. Event-night on-call is still a real cost to price in.

pricing.recommendation: $29/month per agency, up to 10 client sites, no per-ticket fee from us, locked for early members
pricing.competitor_range: $89 to $399/yr per site for plugins; $29.99/mo for Ticket Spot; per-ticket fees for hosted tools
pricing.rationale: Tickera renews at $99/yr per site, so a flat $29/mo undercuts plugins once an agency has 4 or more sites. The lock answers the renewal-hike complaints (r9, r10).

first_10.step: Publish the landing page, comparison page and a recovery checklist
first_10.script: Your events plugin update broke a client's checkout: a 30-minute recovery checklist.

first_10.step: Email 20 agencies who publicly reviewed events plugins, through their own website contact pages
first_10.where: Agency sites found via public WordPress.org reviewer profiles
first_10.script: Hi [name], I read your review of [plugin] about updates breaking client sites. I'm building ticketing for agencies where checkout runs off-site, so an update can't take sales down. Would you do a 15-minute call so I can learn what this costs you? No pitch.

first_10.step: Email 20 more and offer free migration to the first 10
first_10.script: I'll move your client's upcoming events off Event Tickets by hand, free, if you'll try it on one site.

first_10.step: Run a $50 ad test on switch-intent searches
first_10.script: Events plugin update broke checkout again? Ticketing a WordPress update can't break.

first_10.step: Answer, without links, in agency communities whose rules allow it
first_10.script: A helpful answer on recovering from a broken events plugin update, with no link.

first_10.step: Hold 5 calls and ask what agencies pay per client today
first_10.script: What do you pay per client per year for events plugins, and would you pay one flat agency price instead?

validation.experiment: Contact 40 WordPress agencies and freelancers who publicly reviewed events plugins (through their own sites), publish two search pages, and run a $50 switch-intent ad test.
validation.pass_bar: 5 agency calls booked and 2 say they'd pay $29/mo+, or 30 waitlist signups from agency domains
steps: Day 1: publish the landing page, vs-page and recovery checklist
Day 2: list 40 agencies from public reviews; email 20
Day 3: email 20 more; start the $50 ad test
Day 4: answer (no links) in agency communities whose rules allow it
Day 7: score against the pass bar

kill_criteria: Fewer than 3 calls booked from 40 contacts
No agency says it would pay a flat agency price
Fewer than 10 waitlist signups after 7 days
Agencies are happy sending clients to Ticket Tailor or Zeffy
Ad CTR under 1% on switch-intent terms
